summary: Riverside's Google account is spending $3.44M/90d but is significantly under-optimized: $784k (~22.8%) of identifiable spend is in campaigns producing conversions at 3-30x the account's best-practice CPA, led by US_B2C_Broad_Desktop ($452k at $592 CPA with 0.64% CVR and 80% rank-lost IS). Simultaneously, proven low-CPA brand and generic campaigns are throttled by budget caps — the WW brand exact campaign is 81% budget-limited at $2 CPA. The score is depressed further by Manual CPC on high-volume brand campaigns, MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS without tCPA caps on runaway campaigns, and three underperforming PMax campaigns with near-zero Ad Rank. The currency caveat (some accounts may bill in ILS) means absolute CPAs require FX verification; relative rankings are directionally valid.

categories.name: Conversion Tracking
categories.notes: Only G42 (conversion actions defined) was evaluable from Windsor data — conversions are flowing at scale (~115k in 90d). All 11 other checks (Enhanced Conversions, Consent Mode v2, GA4 link, tag firing, duplicate counting, server-side, attribution model, conversion windows, value rules, CTV tracking) require manual verification in Google Ads UI and Google Tag Assistant. Score reflects only the single evaluable check.

categories.name: Wasted Spend / Negatives
categories.notes: The worst-performing category on available data. Four Critical/High FAIL checks: G13 (off-intent search terms active — OBS Studio Download, voice recorder triggering in podcast campaigns), G16 ($1.13M in >$150 CPA campaigns = 33% of total spend), G19 (only 17% of search term spend is visible vs 60% threshold — extreme opacity), G-WS1 (Openreel campaigns: $8.2k, 0 conversions; B2B Competitor: $6.4k, $2,122 CPA). Negative keyword list existence could not be verified (N/A for G14, G15).

categories.name: Account Structure
categories.notes: G05 (brand/non-brand separation) is clean — Brand account is properly isolated. G08/G09 fail: the WW global brand exact campaign is 81% budget-limited at $2 CPA, a clear misallocation where cheap conversions are being turned away while expensive campaigns run uncapped. Naming convention is mostly consistent (G01 warning) with minor geo/prefix inconsistencies. PMax is present but three US/UK campaigns show structural problems consistent with insufficient signal or asset quality issues.

categories.name: Keywords & Quality Score
categories.notes: Only 5 keywords returned QS data from Windsor. 'podcast software' PHRASE = QS 35 (critical — this is a high-spend keyword in US_Generic_Podcast_Recording); 'opus clip' EXACT = QS 55 (low); 'podcast recording software' BROAD = QS 84 (strong). Competitor exact terms (descript, streamyard) at QS 5 are expected and should not be penalized. Three of three evaluable non-competitor keywords are below QS 7 threshold. Five checks (CTR component, ad relevance, landing page experience, zero-impression keywords, keyword-ad relevance) could not be evaluated from export.

categories.name: Ads & Assets
categories.notes: G-DG2 PASS (no Video Action Campaigns; DG migration complete). G-DG1 PASS (multiple DG campaigns with varied targeting active). G34 FAIL (PMax Final URL expansion status unknown — default ON is high-risk for B2B SaaS with controlled landing page strategy). G-PM5 WARNING (three US/UK PMax campaigns at $359k combined spend with 75-80% rank-lost IS strongly implies inadequate negatives, though cannot verify directly). RSA quality, asset counts, video formats, and audience signals all require manual verification (15 N/A checks).

categories.name: Settings & Targeting
categories.notes: All four evaluable checks fail. G36: MANUAL_CPC on brand campaigns generating 23,866 conversions/90d — massively over-threshold for automated bidding. G37: MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS without tCPA cap on US_B2C_Broad ($452k, $592 CPA), Webinar Desktop ($172k, $214 CPA), Webinar Mobile ($16k, $1,797 CPA), B2C Alpha Mobile ($29k, $416 CPA) — no guard rails on runaway spend. G39: Top performers (brand WW desktop, US Streaming, US Editing Clips) budget-throttled while underperformers run uncapped. G40: Brand campaigns with 7,000+ conversions/month on Manual CPC violate minimum threshold by 500x. Extension, audience, placement, landing page, and Customer Match checks all N/A.

findings.title: MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS without tCPA cap on 4 campaigns running at 3-60x target CPA
findings.evidence: US_B2C_Broad_Desktop: $452,396 / 764 conv = $592 CPA. US_Generic_Webinar_Desktop: $172,287 / 807 conv = $214 CPA. US_Generic_Webinar_Mobile: $16,172 / 9 conv = $1,797 CPA. TopGEOs_B2C_Alpha_Mobile: $28,610 / 69 conv = $416 CPA. Combined $669k in 90d with no automated CPA ceiling.
findings.remediation: Add a Target CPA to each MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS campaign. Start at 1.5x the best comparable campaign's CPA to avoid restricting delivery, then tighten weekly. For US_B2C_Broad suggest starting tCPA at $45-60 based on peer campaigns (US_Generic_Podcast_Recording: $44, US_Generic_Editing_Clips: $15). Evaluate pausing Webinar Mobile ($1,797 CPA) immediately.
findings.est_impact: $400k-$600k in waste reduction over next 90d if tCPA constrains bidding to peer-level CPA

findings.title: US_B2C_Broad_Desktop: $452k at $592 CPA with 80% rank-lost IS — largest single waste source
findings.evidence: US_B2C_Broad_Desktop: $452,396 spend, 763 conv, $592 CPA, 0.64% CVR, 79.8% rank-lost IS, 5.0% budget-lost IS. Bidding: MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS (no tCPA cap). The 80% rank-lost IS with MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS indicates the campaign is bidding but losing almost all auctions — the algorithm has insufficient signal to compete effectively. Peer campaign US_Generic_Podcast_Recording achieves $44 CPA at 30.8% CVR on the same intent. Estimated excess spend vs $30 peer CPA: $429k.
findings.remediation: Immediate options in priority order: (1) Add tCPA cap at $50 to stop runaway bidding — implement today. (2) Audit search terms for off-intent queries that are wasting impressions and depressing QS. (3) If broad match is intentional, ensure STAG (Single Theme Ad Groups) with strong negative lists; current structure suggests loose broad match across too many themes. (4) Consider pausing and restructuring into tighter intent clusters aligned with proven campaigns.
findings.est_impact: $429k excess spend identified in 90d period; tCPA cap implementation is a 10-min fix

findings.title: High-performing brand and generic campaigns budget-throttled while poor campaigns run uncapped
findings.evidence: google_search_ww_desktop_brand_exact: 81.2% budget-lost IS, $2.35 CPA, 18.6% CVR — losing 4 out of 5 auctions due to budget cap. US_Generic_Streaming_Desktop: 55.5% budget-lost IS, $15 CPA, 33.1% CVR. US_Generic_Editing_Clips_Desktop: 27.3% budget-lost IS, $15 CPA, 33.0% CVR. Simultaneously, US_B2C_Broad_Desktop runs $452k at $592 CPA with no cap. Budget is flowing to the wrong campaigns.
findings.remediation: Reallocate budget immediately: increase brand WW desktop budget to capture the 81% of missed auctions (cheap brand conversions at $2 CPA). Increase US_Generic_Streaming and Editing_Clips budgets. Offset by adding tCPA caps or pausing underperformers. Brand budget increase of $10-15k/mo should be ROI-positive given $2 CPA.
findings.est_impact: Potentially 3-4x more brand conversions for same or lower brand budget; $50-100k incremental efficient conversions per 90d

findings.title: Manual CPC on brand campaigns generating 30,000 conversions per 90 days
findings.evidence: google_search_us_desktop_brand_exact: MANUAL_CPC, 23,866 conv/90d, $2.43 CPA. google_search_ww_desktop_brand_exact: MANUAL_CPC, 3,813 conv/90d, $2.35 CPA. google_search_ww_mobile_brand_exact: MANUAL_CPC, 2,183 conv/90d, $0.66 CPA. Threshold for automated bidding is 15 conversions/month; these campaigns are 500x above threshold. Manual CPC is also contributing to the 81% budget-lost IS on WW desktop — the algorithm cannot dynamically allocate bids to capture all available impression share.
findings.remediation: Migrate brand campaigns to MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS or tCPA. Recommended: set tCPA at $5-8 for brand campaigns (2-3x current $2.40 CPA to avoid restricting delivery). Test one brand campaign first, monitor for 2 weeks, then roll out. This will also allow the algorithm to manage budget more efficiently and reduce the 81% budget-lost IS.
findings.est_impact: Improved IS capture; estimated 15-25% more brand conversions at similar or lower CPA

findings.title: Three PMax campaigns ($359k) with 75-80% rank-lost IS and <2% CVR — structural failure
findings.evidence: US_PMax_Podcasting: $148,103 / 593 conv = $250 CPA, 1.82% CVR, 74.4% rank-lost IS, 10.7% search IS. US_PMax_DescriptEditing: $119,195 / 435 conv = $274 CPA, 0.91% CVR, 79.4% rank-lost IS, 11.9% search IS. UK_PMax_Podcasting: $91,729 / 191 conv = $481 CPA, 0.41% CVR, 76.5% rank-lost IS, 13.2% search IS. Contrast: DE_PMax_Podcasting: $25,299 / 4,675 conv = $5.41 CPA, 32.3% CVR — same PMax format, 50x better CPA. PMax_Clean variant: $3,908 / 8 conv = $488 CPA, suggesting the 'Clean' rebuild also failing to find signal.
findings.remediation: (1) Verify negative keyword lists are applied — PMax campaign-level negatives are now available and can immediately exclude brand terms and irrelevant queries. (2) Check asset group completeness: minimum 20 images, 5 logos, 5 native videos. (3) Verify audience signals are configured per asset group. (4) Check Final URL expansion — consider disabling if landing page strategy requires specific pages. (5) Consider pausing UK_PMax ($481 CPA) and redirecting budget to proven UK_B2C_Alpha_Desktop ($63 CPA). The DE_PMax success suggests the format can work when properly configured.
findings.est_impact: Pausing UK_PMax alone saves ~$92k/90d while redirecting to better UK campaign. US PMax restructure could recover $215k in excess spend.

findings.title: Openreel competitor campaigns ($8.2k) and US_Competitors_B2B ($6.4k) generating near-zero conversions
findings.evidence: US_Competitors_Openreel_Desktop: $6,677, 343 clicks, 0 conversions. CAUKAU_Competitors_Openreel_Desktop: $1,494, 97 clicks, 0 conversions. ROW_Competitors_Openreel_Desktop: $2,460, 334 clicks, 1 conversion ($2,460 CPA). DE_Competitors_Openreel: $75, 0 conv. US_Competitors_B2B_Desktop: $6,367, 306 clicks, 3 conversions ($2,122 CPA). All running TARGET_SPEND (Openreel) or MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS (B2B) with no conversion data to optimize against.
findings.remediation: Pause all Openreel competitor campaigns immediately (OpenReel is a niche enterprise product; Riverside's PLG audience is unlikely to be searching for it as a consideration-stage competitor). Pause US_Competitors_B2B_Desktop or restructure with tCPA targeting the B2B demo-booking conversion specifically. Combined saves $16k+ in 90d.
findings.est_impact: $16,500 in 90d from pausing zero/near-zero conversion competitor campaigns

findings.title: US_Generic_Webinar_Mobile: $16k at $1,797 CPA with 9 conversions in 90 days
findings.evidence: US_Generic_Webinar_Mobile: $16,172 spend, 993 clicks, 9 conversions, $1,797 CPA, 0.91% CVR, 37.2% rank-lost IS. Desktop counterpart US_Generic_Webinar_Desktop: $172,287, $214 CPA (also high but 8x more efficient than mobile). Webinar content likely has poor mobile experience or the landing page fails on mobile.
findings.remediation: Pause the mobile webinar campaign immediately. Root cause is likely a non-mobile-optimized webinar landing page. Before re-enabling: (1) verify mobile LCP <2.5s on webinar landing page, (2) test mobile conversion flow, (3) reconsider if webinar signups should be served on mobile at all. Also evaluate whether desktop webinar at $214 CPA is justified given B2B SaaS benchmarks — this may require HubSpot/Omni data to assess lead quality.
findings.est_impact: $16k saved in 90d from pause; webinar desktop also warrants tCPA cap review

findings.title: TopGEOs_B2C_Alpha_Mobile: $29k at $416 CPA, 1.1% CVR across 5,985 clicks
findings.evidence: TopGEOs_B2C_Alpha_Mobile: $28,610, 5,985 clicks, 68.8 conversions, $416 CPA, 1.15% CVR. Desktop equivalent CAUKAU_B2C_Alpha_Desktop: $178,590, $57 CPA, 21.1% CVR. Mobile CVR is 19x lower than desktop for the same audience, suggesting mobile landing page failure or the conversion action is not mobile-optimized.
findings.remediation: Pause mobile alpha or add aggressive bid adjustment to drastically reduce mobile bids (-80% to -90%). Investigate mobile landing page conversion flow — Riverside's app may require desktop for signup. If mobile is purely top-of-funnel, reframe the conversion action for mobile behavior.
findings.est_impact: $27k in excess spend recoverable in 90d (conv at $57 peer CPA would cost ~$3,900 for same 69 conversions)

findings.title: Off-intent search terms active in podcast recording campaigns — OBS Studio, voice recorder
findings.evidence: US_Generic_Podcast_Recording_Desktop search terms include: 'obs download' ($585, 8 conv, $73 CPA), 'obs studio download' ($745, 13.5 conv, $55 CPA), 'voice recorder' ($6,610, 309 conv, $21 CPA), 'recording' ($591, 9 conv, $66 CPA), 'podcast' ($551, 4 conv, $138 CPA). 'voice recorder' alone is $6.6k/90d and unlikely to target Riverside's B2B/creator SaaS audience. OBS users are typically free-tool-seekers with very low intent for a paid SaaS product.
findings.remediation: Add negatives immediately: [obs studio], [obs download], [voice recorder], [audio recorder], [free recorder] to the podcast recording campaign and account-level negative lists. Also review full search term report for the 83% of spend that is not visible — this level of broad match opacity likely hides significant additional off-intent spend.
findings.est_impact: $7-10k in direct savings from visible off-intent terms; likely much more in the 83% non-visible spend

findings.title: Only 17% of search spend is visible in search term report — extreme opacity
findings.evidence: Total visible search term spend in export: $414,191 against total Search campaign spend: $2,394,530 = 17.3% visibility. The 60% threshold is far from met. PMax ($388k) and DSA ($177k) campaigns contribute to opacity, but even within Search, many campaigns show null search terms in Windsor's export.
findings.remediation: Export full search term report directly from Google Ads UI (not Windsor) filtered by last 30 days. Review terms with >$10 spend and 0 conversions. Add recurring 2-week search term audit to marketing ops calendar. The off-intent terms visible in this audit (OBS Studio, voice recorder) are likely just the tip of the iceberg.
findings.est_impact: Unknown until full report pulled; given account scale ($2.4M search spend), even 3-5% waste in hidden terms = $72-120k

findings.title: Critical keywords below Quality Score threshold — 'podcast software' PHRASE at QS 35
findings.evidence: From available QS data: 'podcast software' PHRASE = QS 35 (should be ≥70; in US_Generic_Podcast_Recording_Desktop, $11,577 spend). 'opus clip' EXACT = QS 55 (US_Generic_Editing_Clips_Desktop, $27,124 spend). Competitor terms at QS 5 are expected and excluded. 'podcast recording software' BROAD in same campaign = QS 84 suggesting the PHRASE match variant has worse ad relevance or landing page alignment.
findings.remediation: For 'podcast software' PHRASE: (1) audit ad copy to ensure headlines include the exact phrase, (2) verify landing page H1/title contains 'podcast software', (3) check if this PHRASE is cannibalizing searches that would be better served by the BROAD variant at QS 84. For 'opus clip' EXACT: review competitor landing page relevance and CTR. Low QS means Riverside is paying a significant CPC premium — QS 35 implies up to 400% CPC penalty relative to QS 10.
findings.est_impact: QS improvement from 35 to 70 on 'podcast software' could reduce CPC by 40-60%, saving $4-7k/90d on that keyword alone

findings.title: Dormant Google Ads account (Search Ads Account V2, ID 228-244-5778) — zero spend in 90 days
findings.evidence: Account 'Search Ads Account V2' (228-244-5778) present in account structure but returned $0 spend in 90-day Windsor export. Three active accounts (Brand, Riverside.fm, YouTube Ads Account) handle all spend.
findings.remediation: Verify this account is intentionally dormant: (1) check if it has any active campaigns or assets that could unexpectedly resume, (2) confirm whether it was a legacy account that has been superseded, (3) consider whether it contains historical data or conversion actions that may be referenced by active accounts. If fully superseded, deactivate at account level to prevent inadvertent future spend.
findings.est_impact: Risk mitigation — prevents inadvertent reactivation of legacy campaigns

findings.title: Consent Mode v2 unverified — critical for UK and DE campaigns (EU/EEA enforcement active)
findings.evidence: Riverside runs UK campaigns ($45k UK_B2C_Alpha, $92k UK_PMax, $64k UK Demand Gen = $201k/90d) and DE campaigns ($41k DE_B2C_Alpha, $25k DE_PMax = $66k/90d) targeting EU/EEA users. Consent Mode v2 enforcement began July 21, 2025 for EEA/UK. Without Advanced Consent Mode v2, all EEA/UK conversion modeling is degraded and Smart Bidding is making decisions on incomplete data.
findings.remediation: Verify Consent Mode v2 Advanced implementation in Google Tag Manager / site tag. Check Google Ads > Measurement > Consent Mode status. If not implemented, prioritize immediately — this affects $267k/90d in EU/UK spend and all optimization quality for those campaigns. Without it, you may be losing 15-25% of modeled conversions.
findings.est_impact: 15-25% conversion recovery for $267k EU/UK spend; critical for bidding signal quality

findings.title: Enhanced Conversions status unverified — potential 10% conversion measurement uplift unclaimed
findings.evidence: Cannot verify from Windsor export whether Enhanced Conversions (EC) are active. At $3.44M/90d Google spend with 114k tracked conversions, a 10% uplift in conversion signal from EC would meaningfully improve Smart Bidding accuracy across all MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS campaigns.
findings.remediation: Check Google Ads > Measurement > Conversions > Settings > Enhanced conversions. If not enabled: turn on Enhanced Conversions for web and configure GTM/global site tag to pass hashed user data. Free to implement, 5-minute configuration, ~10% conversion measurement improvement.
findings.est_impact: ~10% improvement in conversion measurement accuracy; improved Smart Bidding signal quality across all 34 automated campaigns

findings.title: YouTube_Awareness_US-CAUKAU VIDEO campaign at $4,074 CPA — zero optimization toward conversions
findings.evidence: YouTube_Awareness_US-CAUKAU: $44,819 spend, TARGET_CPV, 8.26M impressions, 11 conversions, $4,074 CPA. This is the correct strategy for pure brand awareness (CPV bidding is reach-focused), but the account should be clear this spend is entirely awareness, not performance. No conversion expectations are valid here.
findings.remediation: Confirm this campaign's KPI is reach/view-rate/CPV, not CPA. Remove it from any performance reporting that averages CPA across all campaigns. If the team needs to justify awareness spend, pull Brand Lift data from Google Ads or run incrementality tests. Consider reallocating to Demand Gen campaigns which provide awareness + conversion tracking in one format.
findings.est_impact: Clarity: this spend is awareness-only; if pure brand lift not measured, consider reallocating to Demand Gen which has mixed awareness + performance attribution

findings.title: WW brand exact campaign throttled at 81% — cheapest conversions in the account being rationed
findings.evidence: google_search_ww_desktop_brand_exact: 81.2% budget-lost IS, $8,961 spend in 90d, $2.35 CPA, 18.6% CVR. If IS were 100%, estimated spend would be $47k/90d for ~20k additional conversions at $2 CPA. This campaign is capturing only 14.6% of available impressions.
findings.remediation: Increase daily budget for WW brand desktop. Set budget to capture 90-95% impression share (estimate: 5-6x current daily budget). This is the highest ROI budget change available — $2 CPA conversions are being turned away. Monitor for 7 days and adjust.
findings.est_impact: ~20,000 additional brand conversions per 90d at ~$2 CPA; estimated additional spend of ~$38k for $40k equivalent value vs current

kill_list.reason: MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS with no tCPA cap at $592 CPA (0.64% CVR, 80% rank-lost IS). Either add tCPA $45-60 immediately or restructure into intent clusters. Spending $452k/90d generating conversions at 13-20x peer CPA. Likely cause: overly broad keyword set with low Quality Scores preventing Ad Rank from competing, creating a negative feedback loop.
9 conversions on $16k spend = $1,797 CPA. Mobile landing page is almost certainly broken for webinar signup. Pause immediately; fix mobile experience before re-enabling.

Combined $8.2k spend across US, CAUKAU, DE with 0 conversions across 451 clicks. OpenReel targets enterprise video production — not Riverside's core competitor set for PLG. No signal of any demand capture.

$6,367 spend, 3 conversions, $2,122 CPA. If this is targeting B2B decision-makers considering enterprise competitors, it needs a separate B2B landing page and tCPA aligned to B2B lead value. As currently configured it is burning budget.
$28,610 spend, 69 conversions, $416 CPA. Desktop equivalent achieves $57 CPA. 19x lower CVR on mobile indicates deep mobile UX/landing page failure. Pause or add -80% mobile bid adjustment.

$91,729 spend, 191 conversions, $481 CPA, 0.41% CVR, 76.5% rank-lost IS. UK_B2C_Alpha_Desktop achieves $63 CPA for the same market. PMax has not found sufficient signal to compete; budget should redirect to proven UK Search campaign while PMax is restructured.
Already paused but warrants formal review: $24,583 spend, 30 conversions, $828 CPA. If considering reactivation, requires tCPA and asset audit first.

scale_list.reason: 81.2% budget-lost IS at $2.35 CPA, 18.6% CVR. Cheapest conversions in the entire account being rationed by a budget cap. Increase budget 5-6x to capture available IS. Also migrate from Manual CPC to tCPA for better bid management.
27.3% budget-lost IS at $15 CPA, 33.0% CVR. Strong performance, high intent (Opus Clip competitor keywords), being held back by budget. Scale budget to capture remaining IS.
55.5% budget-lost IS at $15 CPA, 33.1% CVR. Losing more than half of available auctions. Strong efficiency signal — increase budget.

41.9% budget-lost IS at $4.23 CPA, 89.5% CVR. Extraordinarily efficient — losing nearly half its budget-eligible impressions. Note: CVR of 89.5% may reflect a soft conversion action; verify conversion quality before aggressively scaling. If conversions are meaningful, this is the highest-priority scale candidate.

22.9% budget-lost IS at $15 CPA, 11.3% CVR. $177k/90d already invested with good CPA; increase budget to reduce budget-constrained lost share. Also has 68.8% rank-lost IS suggesting QS improvement on DSA content could compound gains.
$214k/90d, $39 CPA tCPA target, 6.78% CVR — best-performing Demand Gen campaign. If tCPA is being met, increase budget to push more conversions through this channel.

manual_verification_needed: G43 - Enhanced Conversions: Check Google Ads > Measurement > Conversions > Settings. Verify EC is enabled AND verified (not just toggled on). Critical for Smart Bidding signal quality across all 34 automated campaigns.

G45 - Consent Mode v2: Verify Advanced Consent Mode v2 is implemented for UK and DE campaigns. July 2025 enforcement is active. Check Google Tag Manager consent triggers and Google Ads measurement settings. Affects $267k/90d EU/UK spend.

G-CT1 - Duplicate conversion counting: Audit enabled conversion actions for GA4 import + native tag double-counting on the same action. Common issue when GA4 was added alongside existing Google Ads tags.
G-CT3 - Google Tag firing: Use Google Tag Assistant or Chrome DevTools to verify gtag.js or GTM fires correctly on all key pages including the signup/conversion confirmation page.

G47 - Primary vs secondary conversions: Verify only macro conversions (trials, demo bookings) are marked Primary for Smart Bidding. Any session-level or micro events as Primary will corrupt bid optimization.

G07 - PMax brand exclusions: Verify brand keyword exclusions are configured in all 5 PMax campaigns to prevent cannibalization of brand Search campaigns. Brand exclusions for PMax are now available to all advertisers.

G-PM5/G-PM6 - PMax negative keywords: Verify campaign-level negative keywords are configured for all PMax campaigns, especially US_PMax_Podcasting ($148k) and US_PMax_DescriptEditing ($119k). Add obvious negatives: competitor brand terms not in scope, job-seeking terms, free tool terms.

G-PM1 - PMax audience signals: Verify each PMax asset group has custom audience signals (customer match, website visitors, similar segments). Generic signals will result in the poor performance visible in US/UK PMax.

G31/G32 - PMax asset completeness: Check each PMax asset group for minimum 20 images, 5 logos, 5 native videos (all three aspect ratios: 16:9, 1:1, 9:16). Auto-generated video from images is poor quality — upload native video.

G34 - PMax Final URL expansion: Verify whether Final URL expansion is ON or OFF for each PMax campaign. For a PLG SaaS with specific trial landing pages, expansion to unrelated site pages can dilute conversion rate.

G50-G53 - Ad extensions (sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, images): Pull asset report from Google Ads to verify all Search campaigns have minimum 4 sitelinks, 4 callouts, 1 structured snippet, image extensions.

G56-G57 - Audience segments and Customer Match: Verify remarketing audiences (site visitors, trial users, churned users) are applied in Observation mode to key Search campaigns. Confirm Customer Match lists are uploaded and refreshed within 30 days.

G59 - Landing page mobile LCP: Use Google PageSpeed Insights on key landing pages (/record, /podcast-software, /webinar). Mobile LCP should be <2.5s. The mobile campaigns' catastrophic CVRs suggest possible LCP failures.

G46 - Conversion window: Verify conversion windows match B2B/PLG sales cycle. B2B SaaS should use 30-90 day windows. If using default 30-day window for trial-to-paid, you may be under-counting long-cycle B2B deals.

G-DG3 - Demand Gen frequency caps: Former VAC campaigns migrated to DG have lost frequency capping. Monitor impression frequency manually or explore Video Frequency Groups alpha for the DG campaigns ($546k/90d).

G-AI1 - AI Max for Search evaluation: With >50 conv/month and $2.4M in Search spend, Riverside qualifies for AI Max evaluation (avg 14% conversion lift). Requires strong negative keyword lists first. Schedule formal evaluation.
G12 - Network settings: Verify Display Network is disabled on all Search campaigns (common mistake that burns budget on display inventory at search CPCs). Check each campaign's Network settings tab.

G44 - Server-side tracking: Evaluate Google Ads API conversion import or server-side GTM as signal improvement, especially for the PLG trial funnel where client-side tags may miss in-app conversion events.
